invariants: Use canonical run_profile and real Loader/core/session-persistence plugins, mocking only the LLM transport.
A completed tool turn flushes durable events; root shutdown settles before a fresh Context resumes the same session.
Restored history contains the previous tool result and is included in the next LLM request.
identity: Profile identity and persisted session id survive restart; Context and in-memory Session objects do not.
ownership: Profile shutdown owns root plugin teardown; each AgentHandle owns its agent scope and detaches its prepared session on failure. JSONL persistence owns durable storage.
ordering: Boot -> activate providers -> await agent setup -> publish -> tool turn -> flush -> dispose handle -> settle root -> fresh boot -> load/resume -> next turn.
errors: Loader activation failures reject boot; invalid/missing saved sessions reject resume. Failed setup cleans scope and cannot publish a prepared session.
cancellation: Shutdown settles owned cleanup before restart; abandoning an observer cannot discard provider cleanup (CON-CORDIS-CORE@10).
adaptation: Deterministic in-process mock LLM substitutes external network/model responses only. Python 3.8 and current Windows tested; Win7 machine validation is deferred by user. This is a minimal integration spine, not all remote-provider behavior.

rc1_review.scope: Current finite executable provider/consumer corpora, original-browser and extracted observations in the single full receipt. Historical alpha evidence remains historical; no inventory-wide parity, arbitrary ABI/history, paid-provider or Win7 certification.
